subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Irish Coffee: A Foggy Night in Foynes
description: A quick win: understand Irish Coffee: A Foggy Night in Foynes.

hook.text: Irish coffee was invented in 1943 at a windswept airport in Foynes, Ireland—to warm shivering transatlantic passengers.

buildup.text: Chef Joe Sheridan added whiskey to hot coffee, topped with cream, for passengers whose flight turned back in bad weather.

discovery.text: When a passenger asked 'Is this Brazilian coffee?' Sheridan replied: 'No, it's Irish coffee.' The name stuck forever.

twist.text: Journalist Stanton Delaplane brought the recipe to San Francisco's Buena Vista Café in 1952. It became iconic.

climax.text: The Buena Vista still serves 2,000 Irish coffees daily—the most of any single bar in the world. Sheridan's creation endures.

punchline.text: Bad weather, warm whiskey, floating cream. One stormy night created a global classic.

quiz.question: Where was Irish coffee invented?
options: Foynes airport, Ireland — to warm shivering transatlantic passengers in 1943
